title: Mihin aikaan: answering with clock times
summary: Mihin aikaan asks at what time. Mihin aikaan sinä tulet? — Tulen kello kaksi.
targetSkills: Mihin aikaan: answering with clock times
objectives: Ask for the clock time with mihin aikaan.
Answer with kello and a supplied whole-hour number.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns.
Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern.
A stem is the part of a word to which an ending is attached.
The illative is an into/to form; mihin aikaan uses that form in a time expression.

Mihin aikaan asks at what time. Here the phrase asks about time rather than a destination. Use the complete phrase before the supplied clause. Milloin can also request a clock time; mihin aikaan makes that request explicit.
keyPoints: Use the whole phrase mihin aikaan when asking for the clock time.

sections.title: Answering the question
paragraphs: For the whole-hour times in this lesson, answer kello + number: kello kaksi (“at two o'clock”). Do not add a separate Finnish word for at. The numbers are supplied; calculating, half-hours and quarter-hours are outside this target.
A natural short reply to “Mihin aikaan sinä tulet?” is “Kello kaksi.” (“At two o’clock.”). Use the full reply when it makes the person, action or correction clearer.
Correct the offered hour by keeping kello before each supplied number. The whole negative phrase en tule is provided; no new number calculation is required.
The exercises show supporting Finnish words and their meanings when recalling them is not the task. Read the complete English meaning before choosing the question or answer form.
keyPoints: Use kello followed by the supplied number for these whole-hour answers.

examples.english: At what time are you coming?
steps: Mihin: at what; modifier asking at what time. Mihin is the illative question form; in mihin aikaan it instead asks at what time.
aikaan: at a time; time noun in the clock-time question. Aika keeps strong k and takes the illative -an: aikaan, in the complete question phrase mihin aikaan.
sinä: you; subject (who or what this sentence is about). Sinä addresses one person informally.
tulet: you come; verb (the action or state). Use the stem tule- and singular second-person -t: tulet.

examples.english: I am coming at two o'clock.
steps: Tulen: I come; verb (the action or state). Tulla removes -la and adds e to form tule-, then adds -n: tulen.
kello: at a clock time; marker introducing a clock time. Kello before a number introduces a clock time; do not add a separate word for at.
kaksi: two; hour number in the clock-time answer. Kaksi is the supplied number two.

steps: En: I do not; negative verb (marks not and identifies the person). En is the first-person singular negative verb. The main verb takes its negative form.
tule: come; main verb after the negative verb. Remove -n from tulen to obtain the negative main-verb form tule; the negative verb carries the person.
